candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record describes infundibulocystic BCC histology, absence of jaw cysts, absence of palmar/plantar pits, facial and vulvar distribution, and a SUFU splice-site mutation — features that define MHIBCC syndrome rather than classic nevoid basal cell carcinoma syndrome (Gorlin syndrome). While SUFU mutations can occur in both conditions and both are hereditary BCC syndromes, NBCCS is a distinct diagnostic entity with different defining features (jaw keratocysts, calcified falx, skeletal anomalies, medulloblastoma). Labeling this as NBCCS asserts an incompatible subtype/scope despite the shared SUFU etiology.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: NBCCS (Gorlin syndrome) vs. MHIBCC syndrome — both SUFU-related BCC syndromes but distinct clinical entities with different histopathology, phenotype, and diagnostic criteria

case_quality_flags: MHIBCC and SUFU-associated NBCCS share genetic etiology but are phenotypically and diagnostically distinct; candidate conflates the two
